did: Cards essays now speak. A new essay opens with a spoken intro, every card gets a chapter line in the host's voice and narration in the narrator's, and it can end with a close that says what to do next. Home's Kokoro says every line, each card holds for as long as its words take, and the words are captioned under the card. I rendered the NixOS showcase end to end against the release's own Kokoro: a four minute fifty video with seven chapters. The routine is rewritten for you coming back months later, both showcases now speak, and cards essays have their own place in Studio's Episodes.

calls.title: How a card's chapter line and narration are said
options: two takes, the host's and the narrator's, joined into one under the card
the chapter line as its own scene before the card
calls.why: The change of voice tells you a chapter began, and joining the takes draws the card once instead of building it twice.
calls.undo: Give each scene one line in one voice; the essays' words stay the same.

calls.title: Who says a spoken essay
options: the weekly call's host, with a second voice teaching each card
calls.why: Two voices make it sound like a podcast and mark each chapter.
calls.undo: Change the two voice names; each line is said again on the next render.

calls.title: How long a spoken essay may run
options: at most ten minutes by its words, split into two essays by hand
split into parts automatically, as the weekly call is
calls.why: Your ten minute rule for the call was cheap to hold for essays; automatic parts would need the call's whole parts machinery.
calls.undo: Drop the ten minute check; home's own length cap still bounds a render.

calls.title: Where cards essays sit in Studio
options: a feed of their own in Episodes, Feeds and Intuitions
calls.why: You asked for them to have a place in Episodes; as a feed they appear everywhere the other feeds do.
calls.undo: Take cards essays out of the list of feeds; Renders still plays them.

left: The nine essays already on home stay silent, as first served; the spoken versions are new essays the coordinator writes next.
A cards essay in Episodes has no YouTube link or let go yet, since home has nowhere to keep them for an essay; that waits on its own story.
